cards.title: Oleshky ceasefire begins as aid mission faces mined routes
cards.summary: A localized Russia–Ukraine ceasefire began at 03:00 Tuesday to prepare aid and evacuation access to Oleshky, while missile attacks resumed around Kyiv.
detail: The Associated Press reported that a localized ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia took effect at 3 a.m. Tuesday ahead of a humanitarian mission to the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky. Russian and Ukrainian negotiators and militaries separately confirmed that the pause had begun.

The practical stakes are immediate: up to 2,000 people remain in Oleshky with dwindling food and medicine, and explosive mines and drone attacks have blocked normal access. The mission is intended to deliver aid and prepare civilian evacuations across a route that may require demining.

The ceasefire is geographically narrow and does not mean a wider halt in the war. AP reported that ballistic missile explosions shook Kyiv minutes after the start, and city officials said a late-Monday strike killed one person and injured 10; those casualty figures remain attributed to local officials.

The next test is whether the pause lasts through the operation and whether aid, demining, and evacuations actually move. Previous ceasefires have been undermined by mistrust, so implementation is more important than the announcement.

cards.title: ECB holds rates as energy costs lift inflation risk
cards.summary: The ECB left its deposit rate at 2.50% and said energy developments could raise inflation while weakening growth.
detail: The ECB said on Oct. 29 that its three key rates would remain unchanged: 2.50% on the deposit facility, 2.65% on main refinancing and 2.90% on the marginal lending facility.

The central bank said rising energy prices create upside risks for inflation and downside risks for growth. It repeated that policy decisions will remain data-dependent and made no commitment to a preset rate path.

Reuters reported that markets were already considering a possible December hike, but that is market interpretation, not an ECB promise. The official release is the source for the rates and policy language.
The next uncertainty is how long the energy shock lasts and how it passes into underlying inflation, wages and financing conditions.
